source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The owned first update renames selected en-US Fluent IDs and visible Junk wording to Spam, and updates their markup/toolbar references. Functional names remain: the toolbar item is still junk with junkTemplate, and context DOM IDs still map to cmd_markAsJunk/cmd_markAsNotJunk. Exact accepted metadata retains that split. The label-id consumer translates the ID onto the child label; an ID is not the visible label itself. The original preferences copy uses spam settings without the redundant mail word. The owned eight-file change contains no migration script or non-en-US translation edit, so it does not establish cross-locale preservation or a repository-wide identifier rename. Later dynamic labels, privacy copy, stack backouts and relands are separate phases. No UI, accessibility or localization migration was run.
title: The first Spam string update keeps Junk-named functional identifiers
